notes: §1985:XI.4.3.4 GR2: RETURN makes the next record by the SORT/MERGE keys available in the record area; at end, control goes to imperative-statement-1, then 'control is transferred to the end of the RETURN statement and the NOT AT END phrase is ignored, if specified', unless an explicit transfer of control is executed; 'After the execution of imperative-statement-1 in the AT END phrase, no RETURN statement may be executed as part of the current output procedure', with no 1985 consequence stated. SortEmitter#EmitReturn branches on CobolSort#ReturnStatement (record stored at its own length, DEPENDING restored, NOT AT END only on a record, AT END in the else arm); CobolSort#Return retrieves in key order; the 2023 EC-SORT-MERGE-RETURN for a post-end RETURN is raised only under 2023 checking. Probes at --std 85: SORT DESCENDING K1 (S9(3) SIGN LEADING SEPARATE: +010,+010,+000,-005,-005) then ASCENDING K2 returns them in that order, NOT AT END runs only per record, GO TO in AT END leaves the loop; an empty sort takes AT END at once and a second RETURN takes AT END again (undefined in 1985, no crash); MERGE of two files returns A1 B2 C3 D4 then END; RETURN INTO from an ODO record moves the current length (r7odo, [A1Q     ] [C3XYZ   ]). The witness RETURNs A B C, then AT END, in an inline PERFORM.

next.reason: §2023:14.9.34.4 GR3 restates the next-record-by-keys rule, the AT END transfer, the unsuccessful RETURN with an undefined record area, and 'no RETURN statement may be executed as part of the current output procedure'. 1985 states no result for violating that ban; 2023 says 'If such a RETURN statement is executed, the EC-SORT-MERGE-RETURN exception condition is set to exist and the results ... are undefined'. A run-time rule in both editions; the violation now has a defined outcome.
